newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire says anti-Tutsi governor suspended.
newsitem.headline: Zaire says anti-Tutsi governor suspended.

text.p: Zaire's Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo said on Wednesday that his government had suspended a regional administrator who declared war against ethnic Tutsis.
Kengo, in the highest-level comment on the campaign against ethnic Tutsis, said South Kivu Province deputy governor Lwasi Ngabo Lwabanji had no authority to declare war or expel Tutsis.

"The deputy governor has been suspended," Kengo told a news conference in the capital Kinshasa. "It is not up to regional authorities to declare war. If Zaire is to declare war it would be done by the president."

Lwabanji said on Tuesday he had been reinstated by the central government that declared him suspended for his order against some 200,000 ethnic Tutsis called Banyamulenge to leave his province, where they are battling the army.
Kengo said regional authorities were "resorting to passion" in trying to resolve the conflict between Banyamulenge and indigenous Zaireans. But he accused Rwanda of arming Tutsis.
